segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: You will hear a student called John talking to a professor about a design competition he's entering.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Erm … hello Professor, I’m John Wishart. I’m working on my entry for the Global Design Competition. My tutor said you might be able to help me with it.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Ah, yes, I got a copy of your drawings. Come in and tell me about it. What sort of competition is it?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, it’s an international design competition and we have to come up with a new design for a typical domestic kitchen appliance.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: I see, and are there any special conditions? Does it have to save energy for example?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Actually that was the focus in last year’s competition. This year’s different. We have to adopt an innovative approach to existing technology, using it in a way that hasn’t been thought of before.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: I see, that sounds tricky. And what kitchen appliance have you chosen?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, I decided to choose the dishwasher.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Interesting. What made you choose that?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, they’re an everyday kitchen appliance in most Australian houses, but they’re all pretty boring and almost identical to each other.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: I think some people will be prepared to pay a little extra for something that looks different.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: That’s a nice idea.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: I see you’ve called your design ‘the Rockpool’; why is that?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Basically because it looks like the rock pools you find on a beach.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: The top is made of glass so that you can look down into it.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: And there’s a stone at the bottom. Is that just for decoration?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Actually it does have a function.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Instead of pushing a button, you turn the stone.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: So it’s really just a novel way of starting the dishwasher.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: That’s right.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: It’s a really nice design, but what makes it innovative?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, I decided to make a dishwasher that uses carbon dioxide.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: In place of water and detergent? How will you manage that?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: The idea is to pressurize the carbon dioxide so that it becomes a liquid. The fluid is then released into the dishwasher where it cleans the dishes all by itself.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Sounds like a brilliant idea! Your system will totally do away with the need for strong detergents.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: So what happens once the dishes are clean?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, to allow them to dry, the liquid carbon dioxide and the waste materials all go to an area called the holding chamber.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: That’s where the liquid is depressurised and so it reverts to a gas.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Then the oil and grease are separated out and sent to the waste system.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: It sounds like you’ve thought it all out very thoroughly.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: So, what happens to the carbon dioxide once the process is complete? Not wasted I hope.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Actually, that’s where the real savings are made.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: The carbon dioxide is sent back to the cylinder and can be used again and again.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: What a terrific idea.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Do you think it will ever be built?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Probably not, but that’s OK.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Well, I’m sure a lot of positive things will come out of your design.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Now, you seem to have thought about everything so what exactly did you need me to help you with?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, my design has made it to the final stage of the competition and, in a few months’ time. I have to give a presentation, and that’s the part I was hoping you could help me with.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Right, well that should be easy enough.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: What have you managed to do so far?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Well, I’ve got detailed drawings to show how it will work and I’ve also written a 500-word paper on it.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: I see.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Well, if you want to stand a good chance of winning you really need a model of the machine.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Yes, I thought I might, but I’m having a few problems.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: What is the main difficulty so far? Let me guess – is it the materials?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: I want it to look professional but everything that’s top quality is also very expensive.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: Look, projects like this are very important to us. They really help lift our profile.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: So why don’t you talk to the university about a grant? I can help you fill out the application forms if you like.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: That would be a great.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.text: You’d better show me this paper you’ve written as well. For a global competition such as this, you need to make sure the technical details you’ve given are accurate and thorough.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.text: Oh, that would be a great help.

segments.text: Is there anything else I can do?
